mappings.note: Which human qualities the poem urges, argued at 5 marks. The deliverable is the poem's value-burden, i.e. भाव-पक्ष, so LO-5 rather than LO-4. The 'why do you think these are necessary' half has no home in this 2-outcome set -- C-H2.1 covers अपठित material, not a prescribed poem.

Which examples Gupta uses to carry the परोपकार message -- the answer is the roll of exemplars (Rantidev, Dadhichi, Karna, Shivi) with their stories. Content, so LO-4; the item asking what संदेश they carry is LO-5.
तात्पर्य of 'अनित्य देह के लिए अनादि जीव क्या डरे'. Construing a quoted line, hence LO-5 and not LO-4.
Whose praise Saraswati sings (the उदार). A detail the poem states, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
What is called सुमृत्यु. Construing the poem's coined term, so LO-5, matching the other सुमृत्यु items; LO-4 is for plain facts.
What the poet means by 'अखंड आत्म भाव भरने'. अभिप्राय of a quoted phrase, so LO-5 and not LO-4.
तात्पर्य of 'उसी उदार से धरा कृतार्थ भाव मानती'. Line construal, LO-5; the MCQ asking which man makes the earth blessed is the LO-4 one.
Who stands in the endless अंतरिक्ष (अनंत देव). Content recall, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
तात्पर्य of the line 'फलानुसार कर्म के अवश्य बाह्य भेद है'. Explicit line construal, so LO-5 and not LO-4.
What kind of death is called सुमृत्यु and why. Construing the term plus its rationale is भाव-पक्ष, hence LO-5 rather than LO-4.
What kind of life one should lead per the poem (दया, करुणा, सहिष्णुता, परोपकार). A list of prescriptions from the text, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
What inspiration the Dadhichi/Rantidev names give us -- the message drawn from the allusions, so LO-5; the bare 'who gave what' items are LO-4.

Duplicate of the preceding item's stem (inspiration from the Dadhichi/Rantidev names), mapped LO-5 for the same reason. Its answer field is corrupt (holds option fragments '(ग) मित्र को'), reported rather than mapped around.

Third copy of the same Dadhichi/Rantidev inspiration stem; the stem's question is intact so it is mapped LO-5, while its trailing option text and mismatched answer ('विपत्ति विघ्न') are reported as extraction defects.
What must not diminish on the अभीष्ट मार्ग (आपसी सामंजस्य / हेलमेल). Content of the line, so LO-4; the gloss of 'अभीष्ट मार्ग' itself is LO-5.
Gupta's date and place of birth. कवि-परिचय, which neither LO-4 nor LO-5 covers, so the literature competency.
Gupta's lifelong aspiration (to sing Rama's glory). A fact about the poet's career rather than this poem, so C-H2.3 and not LO-5.
The language of Gupta's poetry (खड़ी बोली). Sits in the कवि-परिचय block and characterises his corpus, so C-H2.3; LO-5 is kept for the कला-पक्ष of this poem's own lines.
Meaning of the line 'पुराण पुरुष स्वयंभू पिता प्रसिद्ध एक हैं'. Line construal, hence LO-5 rather than LO-4.
अभिप्राय of 'अतर्क एक पंथ'. Construing the poem's phrase, so LO-5; the sandhi/upasarg item on 'अतर्क' is instead C-H2.2.
Whom the gods will take in their lap (the benevolent). Content of the poem, LO-4; the gloss of 'अमर्त्य-अंक' is LO-5.
What one must not be proud of (all of wealth, fame, kin). A proposition of the poem, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
When Rantidev gave away his last plate of food (while himself starving). Narrative detail of the allusion, LO-4 and not LO-5.
Why the poet urges everyone to move as one and what the gains are. Reasons and benefits the poem states, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Which arguments Gupta gives for a life without pride (no one is अनाथ; God is with all). The poem's own reasoning recalled, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
Which traits of the generous man the poet names. A list from the text, LO-4; not LO-5, since nothing is construed or characterised as a भाव.
Who is भाग्यहीन in the poet's view. A stated proposition, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Why death should not be feared (it is certain; live well and earn सुमृत्यु). A reason the poem gives, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
What you know of Dadhichi's अस्थिदान -- retelling the deva/asura episode the poem alludes to. Narrative content, hence LO-4 rather than LO-5.
Who is called उदार in the poem and what effect is stated. Content of the poem, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
What kind of life the poem advises (त्याग, परोपकार, स्नेह, उदारता). Prescriptions drawn from the text, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
How the poet motivates us to परोपकार -- by citing Karna, Dadhichi, Rantidev and Shivi. The answer is the set of examples, so LO-4; the item asking what संदेश they yield is LO-5.
What you understand by the statement 'मनुष्य-मात्र बंधु है'. Construal of a quoted phrase, so LO-5 rather than LO-4.
Whom the poem holds उदार, in your own words. The substance is the poem's description, so LO-4; unlike the 'मनुष्य मात्र बंधु है' items, no phrase is being construed, so not LO-5.
Express your views on Gupta's statement 'मनुष्यमात्र बंधु है'. The marks are for unfolding the sense of the quoted line, so LO-5 and not LO-4.
What the poem calls the greatest विवेक and why -- accepting all men as brothers. A stated proposition with its reason, so LO-4 rather than LO-5.
What you understand by 'सजीव कीर्ति कूजती'. Construing the poem's image, hence LO-5 and not LO-4.
The reason for Ushinar's fame. A narrative fact behind the allusion, so LO-4; the item asking what the word 'उशीनर' means is LO-5.
Why the poet calls सहानुभूति a महाविभूति. Construing the metaphor that wealth of feeling never runs out -- कला-पक्ष/भाव-पक्ष, so LO-5 rather than LO-4.
Why one God is father to us all -- because he is creator and sustainer, as the poem holds. A reason from the text, so LO-4 and not LO-5.
